prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The newly appointed regional manager (A) / is senior and more experienced than (B) / any of the working executives in this department. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: Latin comparatives like 'senior' take 'to', not 'than', so it should be 'is senior to and more experienced than'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Out of all the dynamic sectors, (A) / the technological domain is the most preferred (B) / and junior than the finance division. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Out of all the dynamic sectors, (A)
the technological domain is the most preferred (B)
and junior than the finance division. (C)
explanation: 'Junior' is a Latin comparative followed by 'to', not 'than', giving 'and junior to the finance division'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The property developer clearly stated (A) / that the interior layout of the first house (B) / was preferable than the second one. (C) / No Error (D)
options: that the interior layout of the first house (B)
was preferable than the second one. (C)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: My father is explicitly clear (A) / that he prefers reading classic literature (B) / rather than watching contemporary web series. (C) / No Error (D)
options: that he prefers reading classic literature (B)
rather than watching contemporary web series. (C)
explanation: 'Prefer' with gerunds is followed by 'to', not 'rather than', so it should be 'to watching contemporary web series'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The creative design layout of this building (A) / is superior and more aesthetically pleasing than (B) / the colonial architecture of the old town hall. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The creative design layout of this building (A)
is superior and more aesthetically pleasing than (B)
the colonial architecture of the old town hall. (C)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: This luxury sedan is (A) / far superior to that (B) / manufactured by our competitor firm. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: No error: 'superior' correctly takes 'to', 'far' is an acceptable intensifier of such comparatives, and 'that' properly stands for the singular noun 'sedan'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Parul is / ten years / elder than / her sibling.
explanation: 'Elder' is never followed by 'than'; the correct comparative with 'than' is 'older than'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Tushar is junior than all his colleagues.
explanation: Latin comparatives such as junior, senior, superior and inferior take 'to', not 'than': 'junior to all his colleagues'.
